title: tune-nccl-scheduling-and-overlap-tp-collectives
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: tensor-parallel collectives (all-reduce/all-gather) currently block compute kernels on the default stream which limits compute/comm overlap and increases tail latency on multi-GPU shards. This change tunes NCCL stream usage and the runtime scheduler to improve overlap between communication and kernel execution, reduce kernel serialization, and make continuous batching/kv-cache prefetch behavior more resilient to stragglers.

This PR implements: 1) dedicated NCCL comm streams with configurable priorities and affinity for collective launches; 2) async non-blocking collective launching on comm streams plus event-based sync to compute streams; 3) conservative stream-priority fallbacks for older CUDA/NCCL versions; 4) kernel launch batching improvements (coalesced small kernels) to reduce kernel synchronization overhead; 5) KV-cache prefetch ordering tweak so that prefetch kernels are issued on a lower-priority compute stream while model-critical kernels are kept on the high-priority compute stream; 6) continuous-batching scheduler guard that avoids batch packing across GPUs when a shard reports backpressure to reduce P99 spikes; 7) microbenchmark harness and perf tests integrated into the perf-canary job.

Checklist: [-] add stream priority config and validation; [-] implement event-based sync path; [-] add unit + perf tests; [-] update runtime docs; [-] verify fallback behavior on CUDA 11/NCCL v2.x.

Risk: changes affect low-level sync paths; default behavior is unchanged unless server config toggles the new scheduler flags. Fallbacks added to preserve compatibility.
commits: a1f3d7e: add comm stream abstraction and priority config
b2d4c9f: launch collectives on comm streams + event-based sync to compute
c3e5a8b: kernel batching and coalescing for small kernels
d4f6b1c: kv-cache prefetch ordering and continuous-batching guard
e5a7d2f: perf tests and microbench harness; update docs
f6b8c3e: fallback path for CUDA<=11 / NCCL v2 compatibility
review_comments: Marcus Lee: Good direction. Two asks: (1) add a config guard so we can rollout per-cluster; (2) please add a perf graph comparing old vs new for 8xA100 and 4xA100. - addressed in commits e5a7d2f and a1f3d7e.

Priya Natarajan: Nit: rename `high_prio_stream` to `hp_stream` feels terse — prefer `high_priority_compute_stream` for clarity. Also add a comment on fallback semantics for NCCL < 2.12. - renamed in b2d4c9f and added comments in f6b8c3e.

Ethan Zhao: Concern about event ordering on mixed kernels; add an integration test that injects a slow kernel on shard 0 to validate no global stall. - added test tests/integration/tp_overlap_integration_test.py and perf job entry.

Author (Aisha): replied to Marcus/ Priya/ Ethan with details on rollout plan, config flags (`tp_comm_streams.enabled`, `tp_comm_streams.priority_delta`) and perf numbers; requested approval after perf job pass.
Marcus Lee: approved after perf-canary results showed stable P99 and throughput improvements.
ci_checks: perf-canary: pass (8xA100 throughput +18%, P99 latency -11% on large sequences)
flaky-tests: rerun (one unrelated test failed once, then passed)
performance_summary: 4xA100 throughput +12%; small improvement preserved for batch=1 workloads (+6%)
P99 token latency decreased by ~11% on multi-shard runs due to reduced cross-GPU stalls
KV-cache prefetching change reduced prefetch-induced interference; tail latency variance down ~22% in benchmarks
release_notes: Improve multi-GPU tensor-parallel collectives: better compute/communication overlap through prioritized NCCL streams and event-based synchronization, kernel coalescing to reduce kernel launch overhead, and scheduler safeguards for continuous batching. Default behavior unchanged; opt-in via `tp_comm_streams.*` config. Expect up to ~18% throughput improvement on large multi-GPU shards and lower P99 latency.
